avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Iron supplements (>325mg elemental iron daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Excessive iron supplementation may increase thrombotic risk and reduce ESA efficacy; iron metabolism is critical for erythropoiesis
avoid_supplements.action: Use only prescribed iron supplementation; coordinate with prescriber regarding appropriate dosing

avoid_supplements.name: Androgenic steroids
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Concurrent use with ESAs significantly increases risk of thrombosis and cardiovascular events
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid completely; inform prescriber of any androgen use

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin B12 supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: B12 is essential for erythropoiesis; deficiency may reduce ESA response
caution_supplements.action: Monitor B12 levels; supplement only if deficient

caution_supplements.name: Folic acid supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Folate is required for optimal hematopoietic response; deficiency impairs ESA effectiveness
caution_supplements.action: Ensure adequate folate status; supplement if deficient

caution_supplements.name: ACE inhibitors or ARBs (herbal equivalents)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May theoretically potentiate ESA effects and increase thrombotic risk
caution_supplements.action: Use under medical supervision; monitor blood pressure and clotting parameters

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium intake may exacerbate hypertension and increase thrombotic risk in ESA-treated patients
caution_foods.action: Maintain sodium restriction per renal disease guidelines (typically <2,300mg daily)

caution_foods.name: Iron-fortified foods (excessive intake)
caution_foods.mechanism: While beneficial when coordinated with therapy, excessive iron intake may increase cardiovascular risk
caution_foods.action: Monitor total iron intake from diet and supplements combined

monitoring_notes: Monitor hemoglobin, hematocrit, blood pressure, and thrombotic/cardiovascular events regularly. Ensure adequate iron stores, B12, and folate status for optimal ESA response and safety; baseline and periodic assessment of these cofactors is essential.
